items.justification: Transport cryptography and API abuse controls address different attack surfaces.
Vulnerability monitoring is unrelated to technical measures supporting human oversight.
Key uniqueness and documented justification for using undocumented components share no objective.
Both apply minimization at a system boundary; A to the security information disclosed, B to the permissions granted.
Input validation and asset disposal at transfer of ownership are unrelated controls.
Verifying an update artefact on receipt and re-testing the system after a major change are distinct assurance steps around one update.
Cryptographic verification of the delivered update and advance notice to users are distinct duties in one update process.
Development practice and sharing test findings downstream pursue different objectives.
Both require the justification documentation to reach users in an accessible way; A specifies its content, B the act of sharing it.
Input validation is a technical control; guidance on appropriate use is a documentation duty.
Recording justifications for unmet recommendations is unrelated to user guidance on model limitations.
Both govern the use of components lacking assurance; A prefers reviewed implementations, B requires the choice be justified in documentation.
Development-time practice and continuous infrastructure monitoring pursue different objectives.
B names data poisoning as what its log analysis detects; A prevents the same manipulation at the input.
Tamper resistance of a device identity is unrelated to disposal of assets at transfer.
B scopes itself to training and test data; A concerns device key generation. Different assets and objectives.
Using evaluated cryptographic implementations is unrelated to providing user guidance.
Communications cryptography and post-incident user support share no objective.
User guidance on secure state is unrelated to internal audit trails of models and datasets.
Both keep a product securable over its life across the updateable/not-updateable split; A mandates updateability, B mandates contingency where it is impossible.
Recording justifications for unmet recommendations differs from obtaining assurance over externally owned risks.
Both require security mechanisms to be evaluated rather than assumed; A the implementations, B the access control framework.
Update activation and recovery is unrelated to communicating unresolved threats.
Key uniqueness and assurance over external risk owners share no objective.
Checking for available updates is unrelated to re-testing after a major version change.
Both require accessible user-facing documentation about the product's lifecycle and use.
Both apply the minimization principle to reduce attack surface; A to disclosed information, B to exposed model functionality.
Updateability of components is unrelated to pre-release security testing.
Publishing a disclosure policy and logging configuration changes pursue different objectives.
Update timeliness and staff awareness training are unrelated obligations.
Key uniqueness and human oversight measures share no objective.
Secure development processes and protection of training data from unauthorized access are different controls.
Development practice is unrelated to evaluating model outputs for information leakage.
Both restrict access to capability beyond what operation requires; A by disabling or authenticating debug interfaces, B by granting only necessary permissions.
Input validation is a technical control; documenting limitations and failure modes is a disclosure duty.
Input validation and asset disposal at transfer are unrelated controls.
Setup guidance and disposal of assets at transfer of ownership share no objective.
Protecting data as it crosses a boundary in transit and disposing of it when ownership crosses a boundary are distinct halves of controlling data as it leaves a party's control.
Notifying users of a required update is unrelated to due diligence on external components.
B scopes itself to training and test data; A concerns device password generation. Different assets.
